question: Teresa Ribera is listed as Co-Chair of the Global Commission on People-Centred Clean Energy Transitions of the International Energy Agency (IEA). However, in her declaration of interests to the Commission, she stated that her work with the IEA ended in November 2024.

Under Article 245 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and Articles 2(1) and 8(1) of the Commission’s Code of Conduct, Members of the Commission cannot exercise any other professional activity, save for limited exceptions.

The rules require Commissioners to devote themselves fully to the interests of the European Union and prohibit them from maintaining functions in entities that could compromise their institutional independence. This raises questions as to the compatibility of the two roles in question, and the correct application of the rules on conflicts of interest and declaration of the external activities of senior EU officials.

In her declaration of interests to the Commission, Commissioner Ribera stated that her work with the IEA ended in November 2024. Does the Commission know if Ms Ribera is still Co-Chair of the IEA’s Global Commission on People-Centred Clean Energy Transitions?
Is it possible to hold both positions simultaneously under the Union’s rules on incompatibilities?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.4.2026) Pursuant to Article 3 of the Code of Conduct for the Members of the European Commission1, Members shall declare any financial or other interests or assets which might create a conflict of interest in the performance of their duties or are otherwise relevant for the performance of the duties. Each Member shall do so by submitting the completed declaration. Section I.

4 of the Executive Vice-President’s declaration of interests of 20 January 2025 refers to ‘[…] professional activities held over the last 10 years […]’ prior to the start of the current term of the European Commission on 1 December 2024.

The indication ‘Co-Chair of the Global Commission on People-Centred Clean Energy Transitions of the International Energy Agency -IEA (July 2024-November 2024)’ thus concerns that period. Article 8 of the Code of Conduct lists external activities in which Members can engage during the term of office.
The Executive Vice-President remains Co-Chair of the Commission on People-Centred Clean Energy Transitions of the International Energy Agency.
1 Code of Conduct for the Members of the European Commission of 31 January 2018, 2018/C 65/06.
